newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Socialists say Chirac "Nato-ising" Europe.
newsitem.headline: France's Socialists say Chirac "Nato-ising" Europe.

text.p: French Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin accused President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday of "NATO-ising" Europe and bowing to Germany and the United States on European defence.
Jospin said Chirac had followed German ideas in a Franco-German strategic concept he secretly approved with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl last month.
The document, due to be published later this month, called for a bilateral dialogue on nuclear deterrence in a European defence policy and for consultation on interventions in international crises.
"This agreement raises problems," Jospin told RTL radio.
"This text shows a shift similar to the one Mr Chirac did on NATO by reintegrating France into NATO without obtaining any concession from the Americans," he said.

Jospin said previous French governments had sought to build a European defence, and then discuss France's position in NATO, in line with the autonomous defence policy set by former president Charles de Gaulle after he took his country out of the alliance's military wing.
"The president has, on the contrary, taken the other approach of integrating into NATO prior to any discussion with the Americans...a way of NATO-ising Europe," he said.
The government agreed on Tuesday to an emergency debate on the Franco-German defence concept after the left wing protested that the document had been leaked to everyone except parliament.

There were angry scenes in the National Assembly when Defence Minister Charles Millon acknowledged the document had been sent only to the speaker and the heads of the defence and foreign affairs committees.
